extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, EPA Regional Administrators, owners/operators of fossil-fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs), reliability planning authorities, FERC, and grid operators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for requests to extend enforceable EGU cease-operation dates under the EPA's reliability assurance mechanism within state plans. Covers eligibility, required documentation, deadlines, review process, and interagency consultation (including FERC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — existing sources that relied on a commitment to cease operating
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism is for existing sources that have relied on a commitment to cease operating for purposes of these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such reliance may occur in three circumstances: (1) units that plan to cease operation before January 1, 2032 and are exempt because they elected enforceable cease operations dates in the state plan; (2) affected EGUs that choose to employ 40 percent natural gas co-firing by 2030 with a retirement date no later than January 1, 2039; and (3) affected EGUs that have source-specific standards of performance based on remaining useful life (RULOF). The date from which an extension can be given is the enforceable cease operations date in the state plan, including those prior to January 1, 2032.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility constraint — not for control-technology installation delays or non-reliability operation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism is not intended for use with units encountering unforeseen delays in installation of control technologies, as such issues are addressed through compliance flexibilities, or for units subject to an obligation to operate that is not based on the reliability criteria included here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this mechanism to address compliance-equipment delays or contractual/other non-reliability obligations to operate; those situations require other compliance flexibilities or state plan revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite — satisfaction of applicable milestones, metrics, and reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Only owners/operators of units that have satisfied all applicable milestones, metrics, and reporting obligations outlined in section X.C.3 and section X.C.4 (for units with cease operation dates prior to January 1, 2032) may use this mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units that have failed to meet these obligations may still pursue relief, but only through the state plan revision process. This ensures public and state ability to assess that units have diligently taken all actions necessary to meet enforceable cease operations dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion to include mechanism in state plans
rubrics_metrics.description: States can decide whether to include this extension mechanism in their state plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If included, the mechanism is triggered when a unit submits an application to the EPA Regional Administrator where it faces an unforeseen situation that creates a reliability issue should that unit go offline consistent with its commitment to cease operations. States may also place additional requirements on units requesting extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggering circumstance — unforeseen, documented reliability issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism is triggered by an unforeseen situation that creates a reliability issue should the unit go offline consistent with its commitment to cease operations (e.g., an unexpected capacity shortfall identified by the reliability coordinator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The situation must be documented; the reliability coordinator or relevant authority must identify a specific and documented reliability concern related to the unit's planned retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum extension duration and relationship to state plan revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions will be granted only for the duration of time demonstrated through the documentation, not to exceed 12 months. Any relief request exceeding 12 months would need to be addressed through the state plan revision process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 12-month cap is inclusive of the six-month extension that is available and any extension exceeding 12 months cannot be handled through this mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC consultation and copy-submission requirement for >6-month requests
rubrics_metrics.description: For extension requests exceeding 6 months, a copy of the written electronic notification must be submitted to FERC (in addition to the EPA Regional Administrator), and the EPA intends to seek FERC's advice for requests requesting more than 6 months of additional operating time beyond the existing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies to FERC must be submitted through a process and at an office of FERC's designation and include any additional information FERC identifies. EPA will consult with FERC to inform its decision whether the reliability risk analysis is adequately supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning Authority certification of reliability claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit's relevant reliability Planning Authority(ies) must certify that the claims are accurate and that the identified reliability problem both exists and requires the specific relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will assess whether the Planning Authority's reliability analysis identifies and supports, in a detailed and reasoned fashion, anticipated noncompliance with a Reliability Standard or increased loss of load expectation, substantiated by specific metrics; where necessary, Planning Authority concurrence or a separate equivalent analysis should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing — submission windows and lead times
rubrics_metrics.description: A written complete application must be submitted no less than 30 days prior to the compliance date for applications for extensions of less than 6 months, and no less than 45 days prior to the compliance date for applications exceeding 6 months, but no earlier than 12 months prior to the compliance date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests over 12 months prior to a compliance date should be addressed through state plan revisions. A copy of the application must be submitted to the state; applications exceeding 6 months must also include a copy to FERC.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review timeframes and decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA intends to decide whether it will grant a compliance extension based on a documented reliability need within 30 days of receiving the application for applications less than 6 months, and within 45 days for applications exceeding 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether to grant an extension is solely the decision of the EPA Regional Administrator. EPA may seek FERC advice during its review. The EPA Regional Office may, within 30 days of submission, reject the application if incomplete or if the reliability assertion is not adequately supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application element (1) — analysis of reliability risk and projection of duration
rubrics_metrics.description: An analysis of the reliability risk if the unit were not in operation demonstrating that continued operation after the compliance date is critical to maintaining electric reliability, such that retirement would (A) result in noncompliance with at least one mandatory reliability standard approved by FERC, or (B) cause the loss of load expectation to increase beyond the level targeted by regional system planners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a projection substantiating the duration of the requested extension with accompanying analysis supporting the timeframe (not to exceed 12 months). Helpful information includes system planning and operations studies, system restoration studies or plans, operating procedures, and mitigation plans required by applicable Reliability Standards. Units with a Reliability Must Run designation or equivalent fit this description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application element (2) — Planning Authority analysis or equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis submitted by the relevant Planning Authority that verifies the reliability-related claims, or presents a separate and equivalent analysis, confirming the asserted reliability risk if the unit were not in operation, or an explanation of why such a concurrence or separate analysis cannot be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This analysis or concurrence must include a substantiation for the duration of the extension request and may include related system-wide or regional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application element (3) — copies of written third-party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of any written comments from third parties regarding the extension must be included in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides transparency and allows EPA, states, and the public to consider stakeholder views on the extension request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application element (4) — mitigation and resolution plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration from the unit owner/operator, grid operator and other relevant entities that they have a plan that includes appropriate actions, including bringing on new capacity or transmission, to resolve the underlying reliability issue, including the steps and timeframes for implementing measures to rectify the underlying reliability issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete steps, implementation timelines, and identification of responsible parties for each mitigation action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application element (5) — extension limited to substantiated increment of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Retirement date extensions allowed through this mechanism will be granted for only the increment of time that is substantiated by the reliability need and supporting documentation and may not exceed 12 months, inclusive of the 6-month extensions available with RTO, ISO, and reliability coordinator certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will not grant blanket or speculative extensions; duration must be tied to the documented, quantified reliability need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application element (6) — identify required level of operation and propose alternative compliance if requested by state
rubrics_metrics.description: For units affected by these emissions guidelines, states may choose to require the application to identify the level of operation that is required to avoid the documented reliability risk, and consistent with that level propose alternative compliance requirements, such as alternative standards or utilization constraints for the duration of the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA Regional Office may reject the application within 30 days if the submission is incomplete with respect to the above requirements or if the reliability assertion is not adequately supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application element (7) — only units that satisfied milestones may use mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Only owners/operators of units that have satisfied all applicable milestone and reporting requirements and obligations under section X.C.3 and section X.C.4 (for units with cease operation dates prior to January 1, 2032) may use this mechanism for an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units that have failed to meet these obligations may make extension requests only through the state plan revision process. This safeguards that units have used all available tools to meet reliability challenges prior to seeking an administrative extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of helpful supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that will be helpful based on prior reliability extension processes includes system planning and operations studies, system restoration studies or plans, operating procedures, and mitigation plans required by applicable Reliability Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide formal studies, documented procedures, and mitigation plans that directly support the asserted reliability risk and the duration of the requested extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism purpose and scope limitation — for use when insufficient time exists for plan revision
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism creates additional flexibility for specified narrow circumstances and provides additional time and flexibility to allow a state, if necessary, to submit a plan revision; it is for use only when there is insufficient time to complete a state plan revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reliability need is identified more than one year in advance, the approach allows time for states to undertake a state plan revision rather than rely on this short-term mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA-FERC coordination standard for assessing documentation adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether to grant a request, the EPA will assess whether the associated Planning Authority's reliability analysis identifies and supports, in a detailed and reasoned fashion, anticipated noncompliance with a Reliability Standard, substantiated by specific metrics, and will seek FERC's advice regarding whether analysis of the reliability risk is adequately supported in the filed documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should provide metric-based, reasoned analyses; anticipate EPA seeking FERC input for technical validation, especially for requests >6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Administrator authority and opportunity for immediate rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant EPA Regional Administrator would approve the reliability assurance application or reject it if it were found that the reliability assertion was not adequately supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA Regional Office may, within 30 days of the submission, reject the application if incomplete or inadequately supported; timeliness and completeness are grounds for administrative rejection.
